title: Robot Debugging Flowchart
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Pick a robot symptom and answer yes-or-no questions one step at a time to decide whether the problem is hardware or code and find one thing to change.

educational.topic: Systematic debugging of robot hardware and code
learningObjectives: Apply a one-question-at-a-time debugging procedure to a robot symptom
Classify the likely cause of a robot problem as hardware or code
Select a single change to test at the end of a debugging path
Match flowchart steps to the rows of the chapter's debugging table
prerequisites: The five-step problem-solving strategy (Chapter 1: A Strategy for Hard Problems)
Syntax errors versus logic errors and the debugging table (Chapter 1: Debugging)

controls.label: Symptom
options: Nothing happens when I power on
Robot spins instead of going straight
Robot runs but does the wrong thing
controls.default: Nothing happens when I power on

controls.label: Yes
controls.purpose: Answer yes to the current question

controls.label: No
controls.purpose: Answer no to the current question

controls.label: Restart
controls.purpose: Return to the first question for the selected symptom

simulationModel.modelType: Binary decision tree (one spine of questions per symptom)
assumptions: Each question has one answer that continues and one answer that ends at a fix or action
Intermittent faults usually point to hardware; repeatable faults usually point to code
limitations: Covers four common beginner symptoms, not every possible robot fault
Real faults can have more than one cause at the same time

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked decision path with a visible reasoning trail
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Step-through decision tree with Yes/No buttons
keyQuestions: Is this problem more likely in the hardware or in the code?
Which question rules out the most causes with the least effort?
Why should each path end with only one thing to change?
Answer No, No, Yes for the spinning robot. Which debugging table step do you reach?
commonMisconceptions: Every robot problem is a bug in the code
Changing several things at once is faster than changing one thing
An error message means the whole program is wrong
assessmentOpportunities: Recorded log trails for each symptom
Challenge answer: Add a print statement for each speed
Exit ticket: write the first two questions for a new symptom and tag each as hardware or code
